answer: Neighborhood closure scoring. An agent's messages propagate through a sparse peer mesh, and receivers only honor identities whose signed message thread reaches them through at least three disjoint paths within the local cluster. Each forged identity must be embedded in a genuinely routed vicinity, so a sybil flood collapses into a thin ridge of unreachable nodes that get ignored. Maintaining that reachability forces the attacker to rent live relays and sustain traffic across a juniper of independent routes, multiplying bandwidth cost per fake identity by roughly the path count.
